title: Video Converter – MP4, WebM, MOV and MKV, No Upload
description: Convert videos between MP4, WebM, MOV and MKV in your browser. Pick H.264, H.265, VP9 or AV1 and a quality. Your video is never uploaded.
heading: Convert Videos to MP4, WebM, MOV or MKV
subtitle: Change a video to MP4, WebM, MOV or MKV and choose its codec and quality; nothing is uploaded.
intro: Turn a video into the format a player, editor or website asks for. Choose MP4, WebM, MOV or MKV, then a video codec and a quality, or leave the codec on Automatic and the quality on Default. The codec list shows only the codecs your browser can actually make, so the choice you see is a choice that works. When the picture is already in the right codec, it is copied as it is, which is quick and loses nothing; otherwise it is re-encoded with the video encoders built into your browser.

features.title: Private
features.text: Your video is read and converted by your own browser and never sent to a server, so nobody else sees it.

features.title: Only codecs that work
features.text: The list shows only codecs this browser can make (checked at 1280×720), so a very large video can still be refused when the conversion starts.

features.title: Copied when it can be
features.text: If the picture already fits the new format, it is moved across untouched: fast, and with no quality lost.

steps.title: Choose your video
steps.text: Choose or drop a video, or try one of the samples.

steps.title: Pick the format
steps.text: Choose MP4, WebM, MOV or MKV, and a codec and quality if you want something other than Automatic and Default.

steps.title: Convert
steps.text: Click Convert. The line above the button says whether the picture is copied or re-encoded.

steps.title: Download
steps.text: Play the result on the page, then download it.

handles: Video in: MP4, MOV, WebM, MKV, M4V and 3GP files your browser can play.
Video out: MP4, WebM, MOV and MKV.
Video codecs: H.264, H.265 (HEVC), VP8, VP9 and AV1, as far as your browser can make them.
Sound: kept when your browser can read it, and changed to AAC (Opus in WebM) when it isn't already. If it can't, the page tells you the result has no sound.
limits: One video at a time: convert it, then choose the next one.
Which codecs you can make depends on your browser and device; up-to-date Chrome and Edge offer the most.
Long or 4K videos take a while to re-encode and need enough memory on your device.

faq.question: Is my video uploaded?
faq.answer: No. Your video is read and converted by your own browser, on your device, and is never sent anywhere. You can check it: open your browser's network panel while it converts and you will see no upload.

faq.question: Which format should I choose?
faq.answer: MP4 with H.264 plays almost everywhere: phones, TVs, editors and websites. WebM suits web pages, MOV suits Apple editing apps, and MKV is a good box for keeping a video as it is.

faq.question: Why is H.265 or AV1 missing from the list?
faq.answer: The list shows only the codecs your browser can make on this device. Many browsers can play H.265 but not make it. A note under the fields names the usual codecs that are missing.

faq.question: Does converting lower the quality?
faq.answer: Not when the picture is copied, which the page tells you before you start. When it is re-encoded, the Default quality looks the same as the original for most videos; choose High or Very high for more detail.

faq.question: Can I convert several videos?
faq.answer: Yes, one after another. Convert a video, download it, then choose the next one and pick its format again.

faq.question: Is there a size limit?
faq.answer: There is no fixed limit; the work happens on your device. Very long or 4K videos need time and memory, so a phone may struggle with what a laptop handles easily.
